Acute Disseminated Encephalomyelitis: Initial diagnosis: tension headache and sinusitis
T2-weighted MRI findings: increased signaling of the left temporal lobe, bilateral pontine regions, left peridentate nucleus, and cervical spinal cord
Follow-up T2-weighted MRI findings: progressive enlargement of the bilateral pontine regions with hydrocephalus and mass effect on the fourth ventricle
New symptoms: ataxia, diplopia, and recurrence of headache
Neurological symptoms: decreased sensorium, hallucinations, diminished attention span, and gait disturbance
Patient became comatose and died approximately four weeks after admission, which is a more aggressive course than typical for Acute Disseminated Encephalomyelitis
Clinical suspicion for myasthenia gravis, which is not typically associated with Acute Disseminated Encephalomyelitis
Brainstem Glioblastoma Multiforme: Diagnosis: acute demyelinating encephalopathy, which does not typically suggest a glioblastoma
Lack of pathological enhancement of the pons on MRI, which is not typical for glioblastoma
